title: Regulation, taxation and ethics in derivatives
objectives: State the regulatory framework and client-facing rules.
Describe tax treatment at a high level.
body_md:
## Framework

- Derivatives trading is governed by **SEBI** (under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act and the SEBI Act) and the exchanges' rules.
- Eligible contracts and underlyings are specified by SEBI; eligibility depends on liquidity, market cap and open interest.
- Clients must sign the **Risk Disclosure Document** and the **member-client agreement**, and brokers must do **KYC** and income or net worth checks for derivatives.

## Rules for intermediaries

- No **assured returns**; no unauthorised trading.
- Segregate client funds and securities.
- Report client position limits breaches; maintain records.

## Taxation (verify current law)

- F&O gains and losses are usually treated as **non-speculative business income**.
- Losses can be set off against other business income and carried forward for **eight years**.
- Turnover rules decide the need for a **tax audit**.
- **STT** applies on option sales and futures sales.

## Ethics

Treat clients fairly; avoid **front running**; do not push high-leverage products to unsuitable clients.

> **Exam tip:** Remember the loss carry-forward period and non-speculative treatment.
example: A broker's RM tells a new investor with a ₹2 lakh income to sell options 'for monthly income'. Without profile checks and risk disclosure, this is mis-selling.
say: Please read the risk disclosure document carefully.
F&O tax treatment depends on current law; let us confirm with your tax adviser.
never: Sell options every month; it is safe income.
No need for the risk disclosure.

check.q: F&O income is generally taxed as:
check.why: It is typically business income, non-speculative.

check.q: Business losses from F&O can usually be carried forward for:
check.why: Non-speculative business losses carry forward for eight years.

check.q: A client must sign which document before trading derivatives?
check.why: The risk disclosure document is mandatory.
